title: How Pieter Levels hit $10M/y in revenue and gains at a 94.5% profit margin
summary: Levels explains how relentlessly cutting costs, including replacing SaaS tools by vibecoding his own, produced a 94.5% profit margin. The savings were invested in ETFs and a few startup bets, so investment returns now exceed his stable $200K-$250K/mo business revenue.

principles.text: Aggressively push profit margin as high as possible by cutting costs and SaaS dependencies.
principles.quote: I've always been aggressively increasing my profit margins to as high as possible, especially the last few years, and especially this year where I've reduced my SaaS dependencies to just a handful of companies by vibecoding my own replacements

principles.text: Lower costs compound: more profit becomes savings, then investments, then returns.
principles.quote: Spend less -> lower costs -> more profit -> more money saved -> more money to invest -> more % returns on investments

principles.text: Invest surplus mostly in simple index ETFs, with a few opportunistic bets in companies you use and see demand for.
principles.quote: Most of my investments have been simple ETFs like Vanguard S&P500, but also a few lucky stock and startup bets that worked out

principles.text: Ask the services you depend on whether you can invest in them; you know their value firsthand.
principles.quote: From then I just asked every app/service I used if I could invest, like @cursor_ai in 2025

principles.text: Lean, profitable, healthy growth beats spending everything to grow, even if the company ends up smaller.
principles.quote: Many people in the last decade told me to spend all my money, either personally or with my business to grow it, we don't know how that would have ended up, maybe my companies would be bigger, but I'm happy I did it in my own lean profitable healthy way

principles.text: Track profit margin and health (sleep) metrics together as equally important.
principles.quote: I keep my revenue/gains together with my profit margin and my sleep score in my situation monitor dashboard, as those are equally important :D
